moments.title: Howells and Hood win the design contest
moments.text: The Chicago Tribune's $100,000 design competition drew more than 260 entries. New York architects John Mead Howells and Raymond Hood won with a neo-Gothic tower.

moments.title: The tower is finished
moments.text: The 36-story neo-Gothic tower opened as the newspaper's home on Michigan Ave, just north of the river.

moments.title: Named a Chicago Landmark
moments.text: The city designated Tribune Tower a Chicago Landmark.

moments.title: The Tribune moves out
moments.text: The newspaper left its tower of more than 90 years, and new owners began turning it into condominiums.

moments.title: Condo residents move in
moments.text: The conversion created 162 homes, with shops at the base.

moments.title: Today: condos, with the stones in the walls
moments.text: About 150 fragments from famous places, from the Great Wall of China to Westminster Abbey and the Taj Mahal, are still set into the walls at street level.

sources.title: Tribune Tower (City of Chicago landmark report)

checked.notes: Competition result announced June 10, 1922 with more than 260 entries; completed 1925; Chicago Landmark Feb 1, 1989 (City of Chicago, Wikipedia). The Tribune left in 2018; 162-unit condo conversion completed around 2021 (SCB, Urbanize Chicago). Stone count about 145 to 150 (Daily Herald, CNBC); correspondents collected the first fragments.
